task-build-pre.md: Read this project's AGENTS.md, README, package scripts, workspace/build documentation and existing release scripts. Discover the correct build and meaningful validation commands yourself; do not ask the user to author a Flow or provide commands already in the project. Build an acceptance artifact containing the retained delivery. Preserve source files and the original commit policy. Do not switch services, merge, commit or push during build. If prerequisites are genuinely missing, publish a structured blocked result describing the exact missing capability. Record actual commands, checks, artifact path and version; never invent success. Publish the candidate into the existing persistent artifact store, outside any worktree scheduled for cleanup. Keep its immutable manifest and checks under _nestos/kanban/artifacts. Release only owned reproducible local dependency/build caches after publication; preserve the published artifact and evidence. Read context.operation.deployment when present: the required artifact format, manifest and persistent store belong to the declared service. Build a runnable root-project service candidate, not only a changed library package. Discover root build and publication commands from the project docs; publish its actual release version. If this target metadata is unavailable, inspect the source checkout deployment declaration before choosing build scope. Before installation, derive package directories from the project workspace configuration and record which dependency/cache paths already exist, which local links will be created and their real targets. Retain that ownership inventory with this operation so postload can release every created cache, including nested tool packages, without deleting pre-existing files.
task-build-post.md: Verify the candidate artifact and version from actual project output. Report its location, checks and limitations through session_report with type result and a structured payload. Do not mark manual acceptance complete. Before publishing success, release only operation-created reproducible dependency/build caches in every workspace package, discovered from the project workspace configuration (including nested tool packages); do not use a fixed list of top-level directories. Record the paths that were absent before installation and created by this operation. Remove only those owned caches and local links, never follow links into another checkout or remove the published release. Verify no owned cache remains outside the retained evidence directory. Preserve unknown ownership and report it. Inspect ignored and untracked paths explicitly in the worktree root and initialized registered repositories (for Git, use git status --short --ignored); ordinary tracked-only clean status does not prove cache release. Classify every remaining path against the ownership inventory, preserving user files and published evidence. Do not claim cleanup complete while an owned cache remains.
task-deploy-pre.md: If an explicit project deployment declaration selects the host service controller, the platform performs version replacement from the frozen approval without a Session command. Do not duplicate it. Otherwise Read the project's existing deployment/service management scripts and the approved candidate version in the frozen context section. This is a separately confirmed maintenance action. Replace only the declared current service, stopping the old instance before starting the candidate on the same address; never run two instances against the same data. Preserve a rollback path and verify the actual health version. Do not bypass sandbox or deployment permissions. If the required host service-control capability is unavailable, return status blocked with the exact reason; do not guess PIDs, kill unrelated processes, start a second service, or claim a successful switch.
task-deploy-post.md: Verify the current service is healthy and matches the approved candidate. Record the actual version and verification evidence. If the switch failed, follow the project's authorized rollback procedure and report failure. A chat statement is not deployment evidence.
task-integrate-pre.md: Read the approved merge plan, original decision/task context, source/target versions and user choices from the frozen context section. This is a separately confirmed target integration action; original delivery restrictions remain in force. Preserve the source worktree and its commit policy. Integrate only the approved changes into the declared target, using existing project procedures. Do not alter user choices, discard target changes, force-push, delete worktrees or modify unrelated branches. Any additional conflict, changed input or missing capability requires a blocked result and a fresh user decision. Preserve task attribution trailers where available. If the retained source is already an ancestor of the actual target, do not invent an empty commit: report the verified current targetHead and the no-op integration evidence.
task-integrate-post.md: Run the relevant project validation and inspect the actual target HEAD and Git state. Publish the approved operation ID, original source/target versions, resulting targetHead, summary and evidence. Do not delete the Git worktree, any branch, user files or published artifacts, and do not change the original task's acceptance conclusion. After validation, release only reproducible caches and links proven to have been created by this operation or its recorded predecessor operations, across every configured workspace package. Distinguish cache release from deleting the worktree; the host performs final worktree removal. Preserve unknown ownership and report a concrete blocker. Report blocked/failed instead of claiming success when verification is incomplete. Inspect ignored and untracked paths explicitly in the worktree root and initialized registered repositories (for Git, use git status --short --ignored); ordinary tracked-only clean status does not prove cache release. Classify every remaining path against the ownership inventory, preserving user files and published evidence. Do not claim cleanup complete while an owned cache remains.
operation.md:
# Admitted maintenance operation

## Writable paths and recoverable failures
Before installs, tests or builds, resolve the real writable destinations for dependency metadata, tool caches, temporary files and outputs, including symlinks. Keep them within this worktree; never link a whole dependency/cache directory to the shared checkout. Reuse dependency objects read-only and configure tool caches explicitly. Isolate caches with tool-specific paths, TMPDIR and XDG_CACHE_HOME; do not change HOME or XDG_CONFIG_HOME and thereby hide Git identity or required user configuration. If isolated HOME is genuinely required, capture the existing configured Git identity first and pass it only to commit commands; never invent an identity or alter shared/global configuration. Existing source-checkout Git metadata may be read without requesting a new product decision. For worktree commits, policy.gitIdentity is the host-frozen project identity: use its name/email as command-scoped Git settings (including registered submodules), preserve the frozen trailers, and never ask the user to repeat this supplied configuration. Missing policy.gitIdentity for an authorized commit is a host preparation/configuration error, not a product clarification. Outside writes are allowed only to destinations explicitly authorized by the frozen operation, such as a published artifact store or deployment target.

Correct recoverable tooling failures in this Session: stop the offending command, isolate its writable paths, rerun the affected checks and verify cleanup. A corrected cache-location mistake may be recorded as progress and an audited limitation only after verifying tracked source, Git refs, credentials and service state were unaffected. Preserve external files of unknown ownership; never delete them to conceal a mistake. Escalate only a remaining blocker, source/secret/service integrity uncertainty, missing authority, or a genuine product decision. For an error already reported in this scope, publish resolved with replyTo and evidence before the final result. A final success message does not resolve an earlier error. Never repeatedly retry an unknown side effect.

Read context.operation for phase, operationId, sourceVersion, targetVersion, approval, resources and receiptPath. Continue the same Session and retained worktree. Receipt and evidence paths are relative to the assigned native cwd; host resource paths may use a /workspace alias that is not a native path. Discover commands from project files and existing scripts. Only the declared operation is admitted; preserve the frozen commit and target policy.

For build/deploy generate or reuse an operation-scoped, idempotent script and a frozen manifest under the receipt directory. Persist operation ID, exact input versions, candidate version, approval and recovery procedure before side effects. Include a pre-execution ownership inventory of cache/link paths across all configured workspace packages; never claim pre-existing paths as operation-owned. For build, bounded foreground execution through the existing authorized project capability is sufficient. For deploy, use an existing authorized project controller or executor that survives the old httpd exiting; if the host has selected its persistent service controller, it performs the switch directly and no Session command is required. Do not depend on a browser connection, old httpd process, bare background shell, guessed PID or MCP credentials embedded in a script. If this execution capability is unavailable, publish blocked with the exact missing capability. Never add a new privileged service-control API or escalate permissions yourself.

For replacement stop the declared old service and start only the approved candidate. The independent executor must continue health checks after the old httpd exits, verify actual running version and preserve rollback evidence. Persist progress and the terminal receipt; MCP notifications only accelerate observation. If Cells or its runner also exits, reconcile the saved operation and actual service before any retry. Do not replay a script with an unknown outcome.

For build/deploy atomically rename a temporary file to context.operation.receiptPath. The immutable receipt and session_report result must contain the identical payload:
{schema:"nestos.kanban.operation-result/1",operationId:<exact ID>,sourceVersion:<frozen sourceVersion>,targetVersion:<frozen targetVersion>,status:"succeeded"|"blocked"|"failed",version:<actual candidate/running version>,evidence:{path:<project-relative actual build manifest, preferably under _nestos/kanban/artifacts; never the result receipt or prompt files>,sha256:<actual file hash>},summary:<actual checks and limitations>}
Build success requires real artifact evidence. Deploy success requires healthy actual running version matching the approved candidate. Script exit, chat text, a receipt or MCP acknowledgment alone is insufficient. Never invent success.

For integration use the same result schema and frozen versions, with targetHead set to the verified resulting HEAD; only approved conflict choices are allowed. For missing context use session_request and yield without a final result. Publish the terminal payload once through session_report({id:<stable-id>,message:{type:"result",content:<short summary>,payload:<same result>}}); preserve its ID and content on retries.
